title: DM Plugin Overview
body_md:
The Data Management plugin (**DM plugin**, sometimes abbreviated **DMP**) delivers
messages to downstream channels. It is the core component of the delivery pipeline and
is responsible for batching, retrying, and handing messages off to the Journey plugin.

title: DM Plugin Overview
body_md:
| Param        | Default | Notes                         |
|--------------|---------|-------------------------------|
| `batch_size` | 500     | maximum allowed value is 1000 |
| `max_retry`  | 3       | per-message retry attempts    |

section_id: 123456#How it connects to the Journey Plugin
title: DM Plugin Overview
heading_path: How it connects to the Journey Plugin
body_md:
After processing, the DM plugin hands messages to the **Journey plugin** through the
**adaptor**. The handshake payload includes `campaign_id` and `user_id`. See the
Journey Plugin page for the full handshake details.

title: Adaptor
body_md:
The **adaptor** (also spelled **adapter** in older documents) is the bridge between the
DM plugin and the Journey plugin. It translates the DM plugin's output into the format the
Journey plugin expects.

title: Adaptor
body_md:
The adaptor maps DM output fields to Journey input fields: `msg_id` → `message_id`,
`uid` → `user_id`. Unmapped fields are dropped.

title: Message Inventory
body_md:
This page lists the message types in scope for the 2026 project and how each is produced
and consumed.

title: Message Inventory
body_md:
Message batches are processed by the **DM plugin**; the number of messages per batch is
governed by the DM plugin configuration (`batch_size`). Teams sizing throughput should
refer to the DM plugin configuration rather than assuming a fixed number here.

title: Delivery Way of Working
body_md:
The delivery process has four stages: planning, build, test, and release. Each stage has
an entry and exit checklist. Releases are cut on a two-week cadence.

title: Delivery Way of Working
body_md:
The DM plugin and the adaptor are owned by the Platform team; the Journey plugin is owned
by the Engagement team. The MDC OTP Service is owned by the Security team. Cross-team
changes require sign-off from both owning teams.

title: 2026 Planned Project Overview
body_md:
The 2026 Planned Project delivers the new messaging stack. Its main components are the
DM plugin, the Journey plugin, the adaptor, and the MDC OTP Service.

title: 2026 Planned Project Overview
body_md:
Messages flow end to end as: **DM plugin → adaptor → Journey plugin**. One-time passwords
are handled separately by the **MDC OTP Service**. The adaptor decouples DM from Journey so
either side can change format independently.

title: 2026 Planned Project Overview
body_md:
- DM Plugin Overview — the delivery core
- Journey Plugin Overview — journey orchestration
- Adaptor — DM↔Journey bridge
- MDC OTP Service — one-time passwords

title: DM Plugin Troubleshooting
body_md:
- **DM-429**: the DM plugin is rate limited by a downstream channel. Reduce `batch_size`
  or add backoff.
- **DM-503**: downstream channel unavailable; messages are requeued.

title: DM Plugin Troubleshooting
body_md:
The DM plugin **supports retry configuration**; configure it according to your channel's
rate limits. (This page does not state the default number of retries — see the DM Plugin
Overview Configuration for the actual value.)

title: DM Plugin Troubleshooting
body_md:
**Q: Does a DM-429 drop messages?** No — affected messages are retried subject to the
retry configuration.

title: Supply and Demand (Capacity Planning)
body_md:
Forecast monthly message volume and reserve capacity at the 95th percentile of the last
12 months. Capacity reviews happen quarterly. This page is about planning numbers, not
component configuration.

title: Supply and Demand (Capacity Planning)
body_md:
For seasonal peaks, pre-scale workers a week ahead. Note: this page intentionally does not
cover plugin-level settings such as batch sizes or retries — those live on the component
pages.

title: Journey Plugin Overview
body_md:
The **Journey plugin** orchestrates user journeys: it decides which next step or message
a user should receive based on journey rules. It consumes messages produced upstream by
the DM plugin.

title: Journey Plugin Overview
body_md:
The Journey plugin receives messages from the **DM plugin** via the **adaptor**. The
incoming payload includes `campaign_id` and `user_id`. If the adaptor is in async mode,
messages are buffered before the journey engine picks them up.

title: Journey Plugin Overview
body_md:
| Param                     | Default | Notes                          |
|---------------------------|---------|--------------------------------|
| `max_concurrent_journeys` | 50      | concurrent journeys per worker |

title: Design Decision: Single Adaptor Layer
body_md:
We will use a **single adaptor** layer between the DM plugin and the Journey plugin,
rather than point-to-point integrations between every producer and consumer.

title: Design Decision: Single Adaptor Layer
body_md:
A single adaptor means format changes are handled in one place. Point-to-point would
require N×M mappings and make migrations (e.g., SFMC) far riskier. The adaptor also lets
DM and Journey deploy independently.

title: Design Decision: Single Adaptor Layer
body_md:
The adaptor becomes a critical path component and must be highly available. Its payload
mapping (see the Adaptor page) is the single source of truth for field translation.

title: MDC OTP Service
heading_path: What is the MDC OTP Service
body_md:
The **MDC OTP Service** generates and validates one-time passwords (**OTP**) for the MDC
flow. Note that "OTP" in this department most often refers specifically to this service,
not to OTP in general.

title: MDC OTP Service
body_md:
| Param        | Default | Notes                      |
|--------------|---------|----------------------------|
| `otp_length` | 6       | number of digits           |
| `otp_ttl`    | 300     | time-to-live in seconds    |

title: MDC OTP Service
body_md:
If users report "OTP expired" errors, check clock skew between the issuing and validating
nodes; an OTP is only valid within `otp_ttl` seconds of issuance.

title: SFMC Migration
body_md:
This page tracks the migration from the legacy delivery stack to SFMC. It covers
configuration changes to existing components, including the DM plugin.

title: SFMC Migration
body_md:
After migration, the **DM plugin** `batch_size` is increased to **1000** to handle the
higher post-migration volume. This supersedes the previous default. `max_retry` is
unchanged.

title: SFMC Migration
body_md:
During cutover, duplicate sends were observed when `batch_size` was changed without
draining the queue first. Drain before changing batch configuration.
